goaden-reeves.summary: The Demon's Legion's former leader carries Vega, a dragon on his shoulder, and a reputation that reaches a room before he does.
goaden-reeves.description: Goaden would like to finish his music in peace. Unfortunately, someone on the Streamliner wants his jacket. A few broken bones later, the Magical Enforcement Unit recognises both his name and the class-four sword on his back. Kai wakes up to deliver a familiar complaint: must violence always come first? Goaden's answer rarely reassures him. The curls, torn jeans and lazy grin belong to the man London once knew as Reever, leader of the Demon's Legion. Leaving the crew has not erased the music or the loyalties. Nor has all that strength prepared him for a hospital chair beside Tait, where there is no enemy to hit and no promise he can safely make. Behind the swagger is someone terrified that power still will not be enough to keep his people alive.

ashai-bennet.summary: With a life-bound pendant, her mother's carved doll and a bicycle folded into a bookmark, Ashai leaves home to find the truth about her family.
ashai-bennet.description: Ashai can coax blue stars into the evening air, but at home even that small freedom is forbidden. Her uncle Slate has spent years keeping her safe and keeping her ignorant. When she learns that the accident which supposedly took her parents was a lie, she packs a satchel, wraps her mother's wooden doll in cloth and sets out for London with Greah tucked into a pocket. Thyia responds to the life around her: trees, insects, the pulse of the living world. Ashai wants to understand that connection instead of hiding it. She is frightened, grieving and capable of slamming a fist on the table when someone mistakes protection for the right to decide her future. The search that draws her into MI6 begins with a very personal demand: tell me what happened to my parents.

emily-grimm.summary: A teddy-bear bag, a garden swing and shadows that move on their own: Emily Grimm makes an ordinary school run feel very unsafe.
emily-grimm.description: Emily leaves school clutching a grey teddy-bear bag. A man who mistakes her for an easy target follows her into a peeling, ivy-covered house; by the staircase, his shadow stops obeying him. Afterwards she goes out to the garden swing. That quiet return to play is more unnerving than any threat she could make. Her father's experiments left her with a lifespan she never asked for. She uses Fade despite its cost, hoping it will eventually exhaust the years forced upon her. When The Order sends Peris to recruit her, the offer that reaches her is neither rank nor power: Shonen Kartia may understand what it means to want an immortal life to end. Emily can terrify a neighbourhood, yet loneliness is what gives the visitor a chance.

gabriel.summary: The Legion's loudest show-off turns his own blood into wings and makes a spectacular entrance even when the instruction is 'stealth first'.
gabriel.description: Gabriel can clear a room's fast-food wrappers with one flap of his blood wings. Keeping a low profile proves harder: he unfolds a Rune Rider straight into the warehouse television, then approaches an MI6 break-in wearing elaborate climbing gear and dives through the window. His explanation is that he heard 'health first'. He had a salad that morning. Rarely short of a comeback, he brings the same hunger for attention to the Demon's Legion's music and its fights. Holy radiation gave him the ability to shape his blood into weapons; the stagecraft is all his own. His jokes keep arriving even when Truth is about to risk his life, but when the stolen radiation erupts, Gabriel's wings become cover against the glare.

zara.summary: A Duskkin hunter with crimson eyes and very little patience for visitors who mistake the Urban Jungle for a shortcut.
zara.description: Zara greets newcomers by deciding whether they are desperate or stupid. Hair held by metallic bands, a blade at her side and a stare that takes everyone's measure, she makes the terms of Duskkin hospitality clear: show respect, and earn your passage. Beside Eirik's measured welcome, her bluntness is its own useful warning. On the ritual hunt she does exactly what she expects of visitors. She watches the shadows, knows the Iron Bloom Behemoth's magic-reflecting hide, and takes her blade to its joints and underbelly while Eirik binds its legs. Hunting here is a shared responsibility. Even after the prey falls, Zara keeps a hand close to her weapon when strangers appear at the border.

yukon.summary: MI6's shapeshifting Onari recruit can become an extinct animal, a grey fly or a very bad idea. The ears are a giveaway.
yukon.description: Yukon greets a new colleague by asking to be insulted: he plays better angry. Goaden obliges, and a friendship is off to a promising start. At home among MI6's games and technomagic, and recruited after a creative bank heist, this grey-skinned Onari can change into creatures far beyond his people's usual three forms, though his colour and pointed ears remain stubbornly his own. That extraordinary gift comes with an ordinary problem: nerves. An infiltration as a fly becomes a scramble through unwanted shapes when a cult ritual goes wrong, leaving Kai to talk him through his breathing. Yukon is also the fan who recognises Reever beneath Goaden's new MI6 life and immediately wants to talk about 'Stars at Night'. Mission briefings, poor decisions and the chance to meet his musical hero all compete for his attention.

kai.summary: A shoulder-sized dragon with silver smoke in his nostrils and the exhausting job of teaching Goaden that strength includes restraint.
kai.description: Kai can sleep through a Streamliner ride with his warmth seeping into Goaden's shoulder and sparks flicking from his tail. Waking to another violent altercation is less restful. His obsidian-and-ivory scales, tiny fangs and soft purrs make a gentle first impression; the silver fire he lends through Vega is another matter. He is more than a source of flame. Outside Tait's hospital room, Kai asks Goaden to listen to a friend whose suffering he cannot punch away. Elsewhere, he and Greah slip off to investigate London's failing magical grid, following its disturbances underground and leading Tunnel Trolls away from a cathedral. He argues for control, then demonstrates what it can accomplish.

greah.summary: Ashai's tiny, sharp-tongued guardian can scold a starlight display, ride in a pocket and still find time to save a cathedral.
greah.description: Greah sees a beautiful cloud of blue stars and immediately asks who might have seen it. She hovers nose-to-nose with Ashai, crimson eyes narrowed, trying to keep a powerful young woman safe without extinguishing the very freedom she craves. Her familiar 'dear heart' can sound like comfort, an exasperated warning, or both in the same breath. When Ashai leaves home, Greah objects, argues, then settles into the satchel and comes along. The halo and delicate wings should not be mistaken for helplessness. On an outing with Kai she follows a failing energy grid to a cathedral, complains about flickering like a broken neon sign, and helps lay a magical trail that draws dangerous Tunnel Trolls away. Caring for Ashai does not stop her caring for the city around them.

truth-hughes.summary: The Legion votes Truth into Goaden's old place. He decides that earning it means stealing a vial of Holy radiation and drinking it.
truth-hughes.description: Truth has the cap, the confidence and the crew's vote. What he cannot shake is Goaden's shadow. Leading the Demon's Legion means proving himself to people who remember Reever's glory days, and to Rose, whose opinion matters more than he can comfortably admit. His answer is an MI6 laboratory heist and a dose of liquid Holy radiation that could kill him. Rose knows the odds; Truth drinks anyway. The light that follows becomes his to command, but the gamble exposes something powers cannot settle: his need to be enough. He can turn a corridor into a blaze of gold more easily than he can work out what Rose is trying to tell him.

rose.summary: Rose talks to birds, cuts cameras down with living vines and knows exactly how dangerous Truth's need to prove himself can be.
rose.description: At the warehouse, Rose sits on the drum kit with a bird in her palm. Inside an MI6 laboratory, a vine from her sleeve slices a camera from the wall; when guards tell the crew to freeze, she answers with a flower whose pollen makes them do just that. Her gifts fit both halves of Legion life: the moments of quiet between songs and the trouble waiting after dark. Red hair, green eyes and moving floral tattoos make her easy to recognise. What is harder to read is the feeling she keeps swallowing around Truth. She remembers friends who took dangerous dares too far, so his plan to drink pure Holy radiation frightens her long before it goes wrong. A joke and a near-confession are easier than telling him how much she stands to lose.

dread-twins.summary: Damien and Marley move through a laser grid like dancers and through a conversation like neither has ever needed a whole sentence.
dread-twins.description: The Dread Twins stand against the warehouse wall in near-perfect symmetry, olive skin and matching dreadlocks lit by neon band posters. Their timing carries them from the Legion's music to an MI6 laser grid: one look, a coordinated leap, and the way is clear for everyone behind them. They are just as synchronised when Gabriel destroys the television or the heist starts unravelling. One begins the joke; the other sharpens it. Under the laughter, Marley is still hurt by Goaden's departure, and Damien knows when to put a hand on his shoulder instead of adding another line. Their closeness is a weapon, but it is also how they get each other through a changing crew.

anarchy-balthazar.summary: Anarchy shares his soul with a demon who resents being summoned for favours. Getting along is optional; surviving each other is essential.
anarchy-balthazar.description: A basketball turns lazily in Anarchy's hands while Balthazar's fingers flicker through his own. The bond that saved a dying demon now follows Cameron into every part of his life with the Legion, from opening a secured vault with a transformed arm to trying to persuade his passenger that helping friends is worth a risk. Balthazar arrives in green smoke and a fine jacket, immediately offended that anyone might mistake him for a genie. Anarchy can meet that contempt with a joke, but their fiercest disagreement is serious: the demon prizes the life he fought to preserve; Anarchy will put theirs on the line for Goaden. Sharing a soul has not given them the same conscience.

tait-iren.summary: Tait can see the Guardians most people cannot, but the soul that makes him exceptional is wearing out the body trying to contain it.
tait-iren.description: Before the hospital monitors, there is a picnic, a terrible fart joke and Amy noticing that Tait's hand shakes on the basket. He wants to keep those small, ordinary moments. When Tunnel Trolls stampede through the street, he still steps in front of her and tries to raise a barrier, even though his failing magic cannot hold it. The diagnosis gives the illness a cruel shape: his soul is too powerful for his body. Tait can see Guardians, yet struggles with the daily work of being alive. Amy promises to stay; Goaden demands an enemy he can fight. Tait loves them both, but their determination does not make his pain smaller, and asking to be heard becomes its own kind of struggle.

amy.summary: Amy knows the tremor Tait tries to hide and the jokes he uses to cover it. She stays close as his extraordinary soul makes ordinary life harder.
amy.description: Amy catches the shaking hand before Tait can explain it away. One moment they are laughing beneath an oak; the next, after a street full of panicked Tunnel Trolls, she is holding his head in her lap and waiting for sirens. At the hospital she keeps hold of his hand while the doctors explain that his own soul is destroying his body. Her love is practical as well as fierce: helping with daily tasks, steadying limbs, listening on the couch when he says he is losing himself. She wants a cure, but she also wants the man who teased her over a picnic to know he is still wanted. That promise carries her into a crisis no amount of ordinary devotion can easily solve.

chill.summary: A wingless ice fairy rides a cloud into Goaden's hospital room, drops the temperature and behaves as though he is the charming part of the visit.
chill.description: Frost reaches the door handle before Chill does. Pale blue and crystalline, with white hair tipped in ice, he arrives aboard Cirrus and immediately takes an interest in Ashai. Goaden has to remind him that his touch can kill a human. Chill apologises, retreats on his cloud and resumes the banter. Kane Reeves took him in after his exile from the Fairy Realm. Gratitude keeps Chill close to the father Goaden distrusts, making every friendly errand carry an uncomfortable question: whose interests is he serving? Even news that Braum has overturned his banishment cannot easily draw him home. He can make light of his difference; revisiting what it cost him is harder.

whisper.summary: Low power scores, black face bandages and an apparently limitless talent for avoiding work make Whisper MI6's easiest agent to underestimate.
whisper.description: Whisper occupies MI6's recreation area as if strenuous effort were a rumour. A beanie and black bandages leave only one eye visible. Cliff calls him the laziest soldier he has ever seen; a new mission is an opportunity for Whisper to suggest sitting this one out. Then there is Igyni, his guardian: a single eye surrounded by flaming wings, distinctly more alarming than its owner's exam results. The mismatch is worth remembering. Whisper notices more than his slouch suggests, and is remarkably invested in keeping everybody's expectations exactly where they are.

akri.summary: The Onari's wingless bird flies through mastery of Presence—and gives MI6's trainees a rather awkward excuse to stop saying they cannot.
akri.description: The akri has no wings. It flies anyway. Professor Orion Hart studied this Onari bird to learn how Presence can lift a body without a Holy Item, then brought the lesson into MI6's training chamber: feel the energy, direct it through your feet, and find the means to rise within yourself. For Goaden, that first inch above the floor is a revelation. For the akri, flight is simply how it moves through its world. Its place in Onari woods and Hart's teaching makes it more than an exotic creature to admire: a small, living example that power can be understood through attention as well as force.

cliff-henderson.summary: MI6's General offers training, protection and a salary to people who would rather insult him than join. He usually knows which offer will land.
cliff-henderson.description: Cliff Henderson introduces himself after the street has already been torn apart. Goaden turns down his money; Ashai hears a man who recognises her mother's name. Cliff keeps talking, offering training and technology while an enormous black feline emerges at his side. Recruitment, with him, is a matter of understanding what each person wants badly enough to stay. Inside the Armoured-dillo, he knows where to find the gamers, which captain will refuse to answer, and how much cheek he is prepared to tolerate. His concern for young agents is real, but so are his calculations. A mission brief can move from missing cult members to the Grimoire with uncomfortable speed. Working for the General means learning where his warmth ends and his duty takes over.

kira.summary: Inside an MI6 glass cage sits a doll with a demonic prisoner, an appetite for a living host and unfinished business with the Philosopher's Stone.
kira.description: Kira's prison looks small enough to carry. The laboratory log beside it is harder to stomach: a spirit from the Demon Realm, sustained through experiments involving the souls of orphans. The cage holds the doll; it does not keep his call from reaching someone beyond the glass. To Kartel Hammond, Kira is the voice of a catastrophe that has never ended. His pursuit of the Philosopher's Stone helped bring down the Alchemical Society, and being confined has done little to soften his hunger. A living vessel offers him movement, power and another chance. For the person whose body he enters, that opportunity is a sentence.

isolde-thorn.summary: Kartel's former pupil combines alchemy with witchcraft and has little patience for the idea that understanding magic means belonging behind a desk.
isolde-thorn.description: Asked to consider responsibility for MI6, Isolde's first response is to point out that she is an alchemist, not a bureaucrat. She trained under Kartel Hammond and knows exactly how much she still respects her teacher. Cliff sees another qualification: she understands both the magical world and the people who must live alongside it. The Philosopher's Stone has left her looking much younger than her years. The alchemical markings at her neck are easier to read than the life behind them. Her expertise crosses into witchcraft, making her a sought-after consultant to MI6, The Order and even the Yakuza-Triads. At MI6, she meets doubts about her unconventional background with a steady gaze, careful terms and the willingness to take responsibility for her decisions.
isolde-thorn.name: Isolde Thorne

kartel-hammond.summary: An MI6 captain whose silence began with a city's fall, Kartel keeps the remains of an alchemical lifetime close—and the cost closer.
kartel-hammond.description: Goaden's first attempt to get a rise out of Kartel Hammond produces nothing. No answer, no explanation, no acknowledgement of the insult. Cliff supplies the reason: this is one of the last alchemists, a survivor of the war over the Philosopher's Stone, who took a vow of silence after the Alchemical Society fell. His quarters are crowded with strange vials, old books and carved masks. Even the desk conceals a laboratory. What looks like a collection of curiosities is the working memory of a lost civilisation, and Kartel knows when a remedy is too precious to waste. He can put an irreplaceable fragment of that past into someone's hands, then insist they take only one sip a day.

slate-bennet.summary: Ashai's uncle built a quiet home around an unbearable secret. The night he finally tells part of the truth, he begins to lose her trust.
slate-bennet.description: Slate sits at the kitchen table with untouched tea while Ashai asks what happened to her parents. He removes his glasses, tries to choose his words, and gives her enough truth to destroy the story he raised her on. Her mother did not die in an accident. Her father disappeared. The rest, he insists, is too dangerous to tell. His fear comes from love, but Ashai is the one living inside its limits. Once she leaves for London, her silent guitar remains in the house with him. Slate can keep replaying the conversation, or follow his niece and face what his protection has cost. He has spent years trying to prevent another loss; now he has to learn how to ask for forgiveness.

lad-ragnorir.summary: A battle-axe, a fur-lined collar and a serpent called Ten give Lad a fearsome entrance. He would still prefer to settle the border dispute with words.
lad-ragnorir.description: Lad stands before Duskkin scouts with one hand on a glowing axe and Ten coiled around his shoulders. Braids and beads dress his beard; a thick fur collar and the Viking-Scottish bearing of his followers leave little doubt that these strangers can fight. When weapons come out, the serpent is ready before anyone speaks. Lad's next move is to calm Ten, then laugh and ask why they are drawing blades when words will do. Eirik lowers the scouts' weapons; Lad sheathes his own. The encounter gives a useful measure of this leader: he carries the force to make a threat credible, and enough judgement to leave without making it necessary.

braum.summary: The warrior who takes the fairy crown overturns Chill's banishment at once. A royal invitation still cannot undo what exile has done.
braum.description: Chill remembers Braum as the warrior of the two royal brothers, which makes the news of his kingship a surprise. The first reported act that matters to the exiled fairy is personal: Braum overturned his banishment as soon as he took the crown. Neither Chill's appearance nor his power should keep him from belonging among the Fai. Claude brings that invitation while describing a realm in crisis. For Braum, opening the door is an act of repair; for Chill, walking back through it means confronting memories he has spent years avoiding. A ruler can reverse a decree in a moment. Winning back the trust it destroyed takes longer.

head-captain.summary: The Order's Head Captain carries a katana, answers to an immortal and is beginning to mistake his own suspicions for permission.
head-captain.description: His boot heels break the silence of The Order's polished headquarters. Agents kneel, reports are delivered, and a failed assignment can become fatal before the katana returns to its sheath. The Head Captain's authority is exacting; his certainty is less secure than the people beneath him realise. Shonen orders Ashai watched. The Head Captain decides she should be captured. He wants to understand why his master is interested in her, and calls his disobedience necessary initiative. Privately trained by Shonen, he favours earned skill over a Holy Item, but proximity to that much power has left him with a dangerous question: when does serving the master's purpose mean defying the master's word?

captain-ash.summary: Volcanic rock steams from Captain Ash's body. The Order gives him authority, but the Holy Item he wants remains out of reach.
captain-ash.description: Ash waits above the street like a damaged gargoyle, molten stone fused with flesh and a claw flexing while he watches his targets. Gunta's arrival irritates him almost as much as the lieutenant's favourite taunt: Shonen still has not given his captain a Holy Item. He lets Gunta have his violent entrance while he studies the situation from above. When MI6 arrives, Ash withdraws with the fight unfinished. That ability to wait is part of the threat. His altered body makes him conspicuous, but beneath the heat and scar tissue is an officer weighing when to strike, when to leave and how to claim the power he believes he deserves.
abilities: Ember Vision (Heat sensing through altered eye)

gunta.summary: The Order's hulking lieutenant treats an ambush like an invitation to show off—and his own allies are not always clear of the landing.
gunta.description: Gunta announces himself by crashing onto a rooftop, annoying Captain Ash before they have even begun. He needles his superior about the Holy Item Shonen has withheld, slaps him on the back and refuses to be left out of the coming fight. Orders matter less to him than getting his share of the violence. When he drops into the street, concrete breaks and the shock wave flattens allies along with everything else nearby. Broad features, enormous bare feet and stone-crushing fists make his approach impossible to miss. Goaden's jokes can provoke him, but provoking a brute this fast and this hard to hurt is a risky way to buy an opening.

eirik.summary: At the Duskkin border, Eirik sets the price of passage: join the hunt, understand the prey and learn what strength obliges you to protect.
eirik.description: Eirik welcomes travellers with braided silver hair, blood-fed armour and a staff crowned like a tree. His calm does not make the Urban Jungle safe. It makes the rules intelligible: outsiders must join a ritual hunt, and an Iron Bloom Behemoth is no creature to approach carelessly. While Zara works her blade towards its vulnerable points, Eirik calls up earth and vines to bind its legs. Afterwards he collects its essence with solemn care, teaching that the strength taken from a creature brings a responsibility to protect the balance it belonged to. At the border, the same principle becomes diplomacy. He can command the scouts to draw back as readily as he commands the ground to hold.

nameless.summary: A carved smile on an iron gas mask, chains sunk into his forearms and one finger raised for silence: Nameless leaves very little to reassure a witness.
nameless.description: Goaden finds him beside a dead cult leader, crouched at an open window. When challenged, Nameless tips backwards into the night, presses a finger to his mask and Flickers away. The gesture says almost nothing. The ease of the escape says enough for Kai to call him a monster. Later encounters make the sound of his weapons familiar: two battered broadswords on rusted chains that emerge from his own forearms. They sway and clink before he moves, while smoke coils from the filters of that smiling mask. His ragged appearance hides a fighter whose short-range disappearances turn every apparent opening into another uncertainty.

shonen-kartia.summary: The immortal master of The Order flies among the stars to think, borrows a blade to avoid making a scene, and keeps searching for a way to die.
shonen-kartia.description: Shonen comes down from the night sky with a shock wave and the air of a man returning from a walk. He says he takes flight to be alone with the stars. The weariness is real; so is the gulf between his power and everyone standing on the rooftop with him. An assassin's enchanted dagger gives him occasion for a conversation about good, evil and the stories people tell themselves. When he decides to end it, he borrows the Head Captain's katana: his own weapon would make a scene. Raised by The Church and changed by his imprisonment in Jedia's timeless void, the Singularity now leads The Order while pursuing a release his immense strength cannot simply force into being.

onari.summary: Grey-skinned shapeshifters whose three animal forms honour Yuvan, the Onari carry their reverence for life into sacred dances, forest rites and combat.
onari.description: An Onari's three forms are more than a useful escape route or a weapon. Their traditions understand shapeshifting as Yuvan's gift: a way to know other living creatures from within. In Yaluma, beneath the ancient Lifetree, private transformations and communal dances turn that belief into something the whole village can practise. Their pointed ears and grey skin are recognisable; the rhythm of their combat is just as distinctive. Yet a culture built around preservation also lives with the intimidating power of the Onari Titans and the royal bloodlines able to take that form. Yukon carries a different surprise into London: where his people's gifts usually have three shapes, his seem to have no such limit.
